title: 1 dead, officer wounded in Edmonton shootout
article: A gunfight early Friday left one man dead and an Edmonton police officerin hospital seriously wounded.
Const. Daniel Furman, 26,was in serious but stable condition and was undergoing surgery. He was hit several times, and was likely saved by his protective vest.
Darren Cardinal, 26, died of his injuries.
Cardinal was hit with gunfire from the officers at the scene, police said. He later died in hospital.
Police spokesperson Karen Carlson saidFurman was shot in the breast plate of his protective vest.
"Right in the breast plate you can see where the bullet hit, and we just are so thankful that that bullet didn't hit a couple of inches higher because it certainly could have been fatal," she said.
The incidenttook place afterthree officers on a minor call were told by a witness that there wasa man with a gun at a nearby home.
The police arrived atthehomenear 128 Avenue and 68 Streetshortly after midnight.
Furman and another officer went into the basement wherea man started firing a gun, police said.
Staff Sgt. Gerry Gunn said Cardinal was known to police.
Gunn saidEdmonton Police have launched a full investigation into what happened and will be assisted by the RCMP.
"The matter is treated as a criminal investigation, which is why [the] homicide section is involved in this investigation," he said.
Furman has been a police officer for two years.
Peter Ratcliff, president of the Edmonton Police Association,told Canadian Presshe had no problem with the decision to send two junior officers into the basement.
About 600 of the union's 1,440 members have less than seven years experience, he noted.
"That doesn't mean they walk into these situations unprepared or untrained," Ratcliff said.

"Their training kicked in, their professionalism kicked in and they did the job they had to do at the time. They neutralized what they saw as a threat, and the senior and the junior officers are alive as a result of it."
